title: gate_verdicts.jsonl record (v1)
description: One JSONL line of a gate-check verdicts file. Line 1 MUST be the header record; the reader treats an unknown schema_version, an unparseable line, or a missing header as 'unreadable' (never clean). 'kind' is required on every record — an optional kind silently merges record types (the dispatcher #99 lesson).

dirty.description: True when the working tree had uncommitted changes at emit time. The reader classifies dirty=true as stale-grade provenance: the instrument itself must be covered by fail-closed.

bundle.description: Bundle directory, POSIX path relative to the repo root.

node_id.description: Profile node claimed by the artifact; null = managed but unknown to the profile.

owner_roles.description: DEC-007 role slugs (no '@'). A list because profile data still carries the legacy multi-role form; collapses to a single accountable slug when the DEC-007 migration lands.

obligation.description: Emitted by the producer since gate-catalog v1; vocabulary owned by profiles/gate-catalog.yaml

phase.description: Reserved: lifecycle phase policy (severity-by-stage, ADR open question 4).

prev_hash.description: Tamper-evidence chain (steward#105): SHA-256 hex of the previous line's exact UTF-8 bytes, newline excluded. Optional in the schema — files predating the field are legacy-valid; from the first record that carries it, every following record must carry a matching one (verifier: `steward verdicts-verify`). The header (line 1) is the chain anchor and never carries the field — its def deliberately omits it, so a chained header fails validation. The chain proves mid-ledger integrity only: tail truncation or a wholesale rewrite with recomputed hashes needs an external anchor, documented as out of scope in README.md.
